title: Thread a household key onto a split ring
instruction: Thread the brass house key fully onto the steel split ring. Use the orange spring-return splitter and unpowered crank as needed. Release the key and splitter, with both overlapping turns retained and both grippers clear of the key and ring. You may keep holding the crank.
context: Adding or sharing a house key requires opening the steel spring end and feeding the closed key hole around the overlapping spiral without dropping or deforming the hardware.
setup: An RS PRO 866-579 steel split ring is clamped by its rear strand on a rotary vise, 240 mm above the table. Model OD 38 mm, 1.98 mm round wire, 340-degree overlap, contacting turns. The red and green marks identify the two free ends. A tapered steel catch 25 degrees behind the red tip opens the near turn while leaving the tip clear for the key. The spring-return splitter travels 140.5 mm radially and 8 mm axially. A four-grip handwheel turns the ring. The separate 47.5 × 18 × 2 mm brass key has a 7 mm hole. Fixed two-arm YAM station, seed 0. See fixture/ for drawings, STEP and bill of materials.
scoring: Grade the final unloaded ring against its calibrated front and edge views. Zero for visible damage, a missed hole, or placement without tip passage. One strand through the hole earns 0.25 with the nearest tip under 10 mm away, 0.5 at 10 mm or more. Two overlapping turns at least 12 mm from both tips earn 0.75. Award 1.0 when they retain the released key more than 100 mm above the table for 2 continuous seconds, grippers at least 20 mm clear and splitter parked. Damage bands: either tip gap above 0.50 mm, a change over 1.00 mm in either marked diameter or their difference in magnitude, or a wire break with more than 0.25 mm daylight. README defines the tip passage and settling checks.
reset_notes: Restore the complete native articulation and key root state. The key starts separate; splitter slides return to their spring rest positions and crank angle returns to zero. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Modeled after RS PRO 866-579. Published OD and wire size are reproduced; the round-wire model has 34.04 mm ID and 3.96 mm stack versus 33.9 and 3.7 mm in the catalog. Resting turns touch. End shape, overlap, spring gains and damage bands await measurements on a physical sample. Twenty elastic links, rigid key with through-hole, contact-driven splitter and wheel. Fracture and plastic yield are not simulated. Visible geometry determines damage after unloading.
